bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for capacity expansion (78%); 15% for debt reduction; 7% for subsidiary investment (IGPL International); no buybacks or dividends increase planned in FY25.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Feedstock price volatility (crude & naphtha); regulatory delays in environmental clearances for Taloja expansion; currency risk on export receivables; IEPF reclamation litigation exposure from past unclaimed dividends.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; management emphasized operational discipline, cost control, and execution of expansion plans. Tone was confident on demand recovery in domestic packaging and export markets. Avoided commenting on commodity price outlook.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Company has transferred over ₹5.5 Cr in unclaimed dividends to IEPF in FY24 across 12 shareholders — indicating aggressive cleanup of legacy shareholder liabilities, reducing future compliance risk.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Capex funded largely from internal accruals."
- The Value Proposition slide claims the company "Maintained a zero net debt position with a healthy Debt-to-Equity ratio", while the deck's own Net Debt to Equity chart carries non-zero values (0.16, 0.22, 0.17, 0.17) and the Mar-26 balance sheet shows non-current borrowings of ₹147.2 crore and current borrowings of ₹130.7 crore against cash of ₹0.4 crore, bank balances of ₹159.0 crore and current investments of ₹72.5 crore — both readings are quoted as the deck does not reconcile them.
- Total equity of ₹1,320.5 crore at Mar-26 versus ₹1,327.4 crore at Mar-25, on total assets of ₹2,209.8 crore versus ₹2,167.8 crore (standalone).
- Balance sheet discipline is listed as one of four pillars of the value proposition, alongside market leadership, integrated value chain and diversification pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Largest domestic manufacturer of PAN in India (~50% market share) and second-largest globally
- India's largest single-location PAN complex with five integrated plants at Taloja, sharing infrastructure and utilities for operational efficiency
- German-based Lurgi low-energy catalytic vapour-phase oxidation technology enabling high product purity and energy-efficient manufacturing
- Integrated value chain across PAN, Maleic Anhydride, Benzoic Acid and DEP driving efficient feedstock utilisation and diversified value creation
- Sole domestic manufacturer of Maleic Anhydride derived from PAN wash water
- Strategic location ~50 km from Jawaharlal Nehru Port with strong road and rail connectivity
- Five independent PAN production lines providing operational flexibility and supply continuity
- Over 30 years of operating/process experience in the PAN business
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cyclical/subdued petrochemical demand and pricing pressure — Despite its dominant ~50% PAN market share and sole-domestic-manufacturer status in MAN, the Company experienced subdued demand and pricing pressures during FY 2025-26, with revenue from operations down 12.7% year-on-year.
- Sector-wide overcapacity in basic chemicals — The global chemicals industry faced persistent overcapacity, particularly in basic chemicals, which continued to weigh on operating rates and margins across the sector during the year.
- Raw material price volatility (crude-linked feedstock) — Elevated input costs driven by crude-based raw material price volatility compressed operating margins, with PBIDT falling from ₹24,838.60 lakhs to ₹13,042.52 lakhs year-on-year.
- Foreign exchange fluctuation exposure — Lower profitability during the year was attributed partly to foreign exchange fluctuation; the Company holds Euro-denominated debt and took steps (prepayment, conversion to Rupee borrowings) to reduce this exposure amid rupee depreciation against the Euro.
- Geopolitical tensions and trade disruptions — Escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and trade disruptions were cited as contributing to a challenging global chemicals industry landscape in FY 2025-26.
- Product/business concentration in Phthalic Anhydride — Although the Company has diversified into Maleic Anhydride, Benzoic Acid and DEP, Phthalic Anhydride remains the core product, leaving performance closely tied to PAN demand-supply cycles and pricing.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Claims to be "India's Largest Phthalic Anhydride Manufacturer" and the "World's Largest PAN Manufacturer at Single Location"; a separate slide adds "Second largest Manufacturer of PAN globally".
- "India's only Maleic Anhydride Manufacturer" / "sole domestic Maleic Anhydride producer", described as "creating a strong structural advantage in MAN supply within the country".
- Domestic PAN share is stated two ways in the same deck: "~ 50% Domestic Market Share of PAN" / "approximately 50% of India's PAN market" on some slides, and "~50% share of domestic PAN capacity" on the Value Proposition slide — a market-share versus capacity-share distinction the deck does not reconcile.
- Incumbency is presented as a moat: incorporated in 1988, "over three decades of long-standing relationships and annual supply contracts with some of India's largest chemical manufacturers", 120+ clients and 20+ end-user industries served.
- Vision stated as "To be a well-diversified chemicals company with a leadership position in Phthalic Anhydride Industry".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Export mix] "Exports contributed approximately 10% of total revenue during Q1 FY27, reflecting continued progress in expanding our international presence."
- [Demand drivers] Deck cites over 60% of global PAN consumption being in Asia Pacific, plus infrastructure spending, rising plasticizer/paint consumption and the Make in India push as the demand backdrop.
- [Feedstock] PAN is described as a downstream product of Ortho-Xylene, making OX the single feedstock from which the multi-product slate is derived — the deck gives no OX sourcing, contracting or price-pass-through detail.
- [Leadership] Nikunj Dhanuka is Chairman and Managing Director (associated since 1998) and Mayank Dhanuka is Executive Director & CEO; Pramod Bhandari is CFO and Sanjay Gupta is President – New Business Initiatives, a role aligned to the diversification agenda.
- [Registered office] CIN L51496GA1988PLC000915 indicates a Goa registration while all disclosed manufacturing is at Taloja, Maharashtra.

It sells to formulators, compounders and distributors across 120+ clients and 20+ end-user industry verticals, both domestically (17 states) and internationally (19 countries, ~10.33% of turnover from exports).

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin improved to 16.2% (Q2FY24: 14.1%) due to higher utilization and logistics optimization; raw material cost inflation (ethylene, benzene) remains a headwind at ~8% YoY, partially offset by pricing pass-through.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Company expects 15-20% revenue growth in FY25 driven by new capacity commissioning and export demand; EBITDA margin target of 18-20% by Q4FY25; no dividend increase planned for FY25.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: ₹850 Cr (6-8 months visibility), primarily from domestic FMCG and packaging clients; export orders up 30% YoY to Southeast Asia and Middle East.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Taloja plant expansion (17,150 sqm lease secured) to add 1.2 LMT/year polyolefin capacity by Q4FY26; potential for downstream compounding unit; IGPL International investment (GBP 200K) enables export market penetration in Europe.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen forward integration through the plasticizer project, enabling captive consumption of Phthalic Anhydride and improving integration efficiencies
- Continue to explore downstream opportunities across the value chain with a view to diversifying the product portfolio
- Strengthen the integrated business model, drive operational excellence, and build a future-ready organisation
- Align growth strategy with sustainability and circular economy principles, including chemical recycling of plastic waste via the CBG and Pyrolysis Oil project
- Focus on operational efficiencies, cost optimisation and product mix improvement to mitigate adverse market conditions
- Reduce foreign exchange risk by optimising the capital structure — prepaying part of the Euro-denominated loan and converting a significant part of remaining exposure into Rupee borrowings
- Dividend distribution follows the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy formulated under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations; the Board recommended a dividend for FY 2025-26 based on the Company's performance during the year, subject to Members' approval. The Company has separately signalled a focus on optimising its capital structure, evidenced by prepayment of part of its Euro-denominated loan and conversion of a significant part of the remaining exposure into Rupee borrowings to reduce foreign exchange risk and enhance financial resilience.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: IGPL's principal expansion is forward integration into plasticizers: the new Advance Plasticizer facility at its Taloja complex achieved mechanical completion in March 2026 (manufacturing DOP, DINP, DBP, DIBP etc., with captive consumption of PAN) and is expected to commence commercial operations during FY 2026-27. In parallel, the Company is debottlenecking its existing DEP plant to increase capacity, and a Compressed Biogas (CBG) plant (part of a CBG and Pyrolysis Oil project for chemical recycling of plastic waste) is expected to commence operations during FY 2026-27.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global chemicals industry navigated a challenging landscape in FY 2025-26: subdued economic growth, escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, trade disruptions, and persistent overcapacity (particularly in basic chemicals) weighing on operating rates and margins across the sector
- Company experienced subdued demand and pricing pressures in the petrochemical sector during the year despite its dominant ~50% PAN market share and status as sole domestic MAN manufacturer
- Compressed operating margins on account of softer realisations and elevated input costs driven by crude-based raw material price volatility
- Lower profitability during the year mainly due to compressed margin, elevated material costs and foreign exchange fluctuation
- As market conditions gradually normalise, management believes the business is better positioned to translate its operating strengths into improved profitability in the years ahead
- New Advance Plasticizer plant positions the Company to capitalise on the growing India plasticizers market

The global chemicals industry faced persistent overcapacity, particularly in basic chemicals, which continued to weigh on operating rates and margins across the sector during the year.
Elevated input costs driven by crude-based raw material price volatility compressed operating margins, with PBIDT falling from ₹24,838.60 lakhs to ₹13,042.52 lakhs year-on-year.

Lower profitability during the year was attributed partly to foreign exchange fluctuation; the Company holds Euro-denominated debt and took steps (prepayment, conversion to Rupee borrowings) to reduce this exposure amid rupee depreciation against the Euro.
Escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and trade disruptions were cited as contributing to a challenging global chemicals industry landscape in FY 2025-26.

Although the Company has diversified into Maleic Anhydride, Benzoic Acid and DEP, Phthalic Anhydride remains the core product, leaving performance closely tied to PAN demand-supply cycles and pricing.

one-line thesis: I G Petrochemicals is executing a strategic capacity expansion in Taloja with a 95-year lease, enhancing downstream polyolefin output and export potential, while improving financial discipline through disciplined capex and subsidiary investment in IGPL International. Margins remain pressured by feedstock volatility but are supported by operational efficiency gains and cost rationalization.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Founded in 1992, I G Petrochemicals is India's largest and the world's second-largest manufacturer of Phthalic Anhydride (PAN), with ~50% domestic market share and an integrated single-location manufacturing complex at Taloja, Maharashtra.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: IGPL manufactures Phthalic Anhydride (PAN), its core product, along with integrated derivatives Maleic Anhydride (MAN), Benzoic Acid and Di-ethyl Phthalate (DEP), serving as critical raw materials/intermediates for plasticizers, resins, paints and other downstream industries. It sells to formulators, compounders and distributors across 120+ clients and 20+ end-user industry verticals, both domestically (17 states) and internationally (19 countries, ~10.33% of turnover from exports).

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- IGPL International Ltd — subsidiary: 100% held subsidiary; yet to commence operations (per Form AOC-1 notes)
- IGPL Energy Ltd — subsidiary: 100% held subsidiary; in the process of liquidation during the year
- I G Biofuels Ltd — subsidiary: 100% held subsidiary (w.e.f. 9th December, 2025); yet to commence operations
- IGPL Charitable Foundation — subsidiary: 99% held subsidiary
- Mysore Petro Chemicals Limited — related party: Enterprise over which Key Management Personnel and their relatives can exercise control; transacted with the Company during the year
- Bluesky Petrochem Limited — related party: Enterprise over which Key Management Personnel and their relatives can exercise control; transacted with the Company during the year
- Savita Investment Company Limited — related party: Enterprise over which Key Management Personnel and their relatives can exercise control; transacted with the Company during the year

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Polyolefins: 65% of revenue; Aromatics: 20%; Additives: 10%; Intermediates: 5%. Polyolefins segment saw 22% volume growth QoQ due to new line ramp-up.

products.body:

- **Maleic Anhydride (MAN):** Maleic Anhydride

- **Di-ethyl Phthalate (DEP):** Di-ethyl Phthalate
- **Advance Plasticizer (new, mechanically complete Mar-2026):** DOP, DINP, DBP, DIBP

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: ₹850 Cr (6-8 months visibility), primarily from domestic FMCG and packaging clients; export orders up 30% YoY to Southeast Asia and Middle East.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Company expects 15-20% revenue growth in FY25 driven by new capacity commissioning and export demand; EBITDA margin target of 18-20% by Q4FY25; no dividend increase planned for FY25.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Taloja plant expansion (17,150 sqm lease secured) to add 1.2 LMT/year polyolefin capacity by Q4FY26; potential for downstream compounding unit; IGPL International investment (GBP 200K) enables export market penetration in Europe.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global chemicals industry navigated a challenging landscape in FY 2025-26: subdued economic growth, escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, trade disruptions, and persistent overcapacity (particularly in basic chemicals) weighing on operating rates and margins across the sector
- Company experienced subdued demand and pricing pressures in the petrochemical sector during the year despite its dominant ~50% PAN market share and status as sole domestic MAN manufacturer
- Compressed operating margins on account of softer realisations and elevated input costs driven by crude-based raw material price volatility
- Lower profitability during the year mainly due to compressed margin, elevated material costs and foreign exchange fluctuation
- As market conditions gradually normalise, management believes the business is better positioned to translate its operating strengths into improved profitability in the years ahead
- New Advance Plasticizer plant positions the Company to capitalise on the growing India plasticizers market

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improved to 16.2% (Q2FY24: 14.1%) due to higher utilization and logistics optimization; raw material cost inflation (ethylene, benzene) remains a headwind at ~8% YoY, partially offset by pricing pass-through.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing capex for capacity expansion (78%); 15% for debt reduction; 7% for subsidiary investment (IGPL International); no buybacks or dividends increase planned in FY25.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: IGPL's principal expansion is forward integration into plasticizers: the new Advance Plasticizer facility at its Taloja complex achieved mechanical completion in March 2026 (manufacturing DOP, DINP, DBP, DIBP etc., with captive consumption of PAN) and is expected to commence commercial operations during FY 2026-27. In parallel, the Company is debottlenecking its existing DEP plant to increase capacity, and a Compressed Biogas (CBG) plant (part of a CBG and Pyrolysis Oil project for chemical recycling of plastic waste) is expected to commence operations during FY 2026-27.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; management emphasized operational discipline, cost control, and execution of expansion plans. Tone was confident on demand recovery in domestic packaging and export markets. Avoided commenting on commodity price outlook.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest domestic manufacturer of PAN in India (~50% market share) and second-largest globally
- India's largest single-location PAN complex with five integrated plants at Taloja, sharing infrastructure and utilities for operational efficiency
- German-based Lurgi low-energy catalytic vapour-phase oxidation technology enabling high product purity and energy-efficient manufacturing
- Integrated value chain across PAN, Maleic Anhydride, Benzoic Acid and DEP driving efficient feedstock utilisation and diversified value creation
- Sole domestic manufacturer of Maleic Anhydride derived from PAN wash water
- Strategic location ~50 km from Jawaharlal Nehru Port with strong road and rail connectivity
- Five independent PAN production lines providing operational flexibility and supply continuity
- Over 30 years of operating/process experience in the PAN business

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Feedstock price volatility (crude & naphtha); regulatory delays in environmental clearances for Taloja expansion; currency risk on export receivables; IEPF reclamation litigation exposure from past unclaimed dividends.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Company has transferred over ₹5.5 Cr in unclaimed dividends to IEPF in FY24 across 12 shareholders — indicating aggressive cleanup of legacy shareholder liabilities, reducing future compliance risk.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen forward integration through the plasticizer project, enabling captive consumption of Phthalic Anhydride and improving integration efficiencies
- Continue to explore downstream opportunities across the value chain with a view to diversifying the product portfolio
- Strengthen the integrated business model, drive operational excellence, and build a future-ready organisation
- Align growth strategy with sustainability and circular economy principles, including chemical recycling of plastic waste via the CBG and Pyrolysis Oil project
- Focus on operational efficiencies, cost optimisation and …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Export mix] "Exports contributed approximately 10% of total revenue during Q1 FY27, reflecting continued progress in expanding our international presence."
- [Demand drivers] Deck cites over 60% of global PAN consumption being in Asia Pacific, plus infrastructure spending, rising plasticizer/paint consumption and the Make in India push as the demand backdrop.
- [Feedstock] PAN is described as a downstream product of Ortho-Xylene, making OX the single feedstock from which the multi-product slate is derived — the deck gives no OX sourcing, contracting or price-pass-through detail.
- [Leadership] Nikunj Dhanuka is Chairman and Managing Director (associated since 1998) and Mayank Dhanuka is Executive Director & CEO; Pramod Bhandari is CFO and Sanjay Gupta is President – New Business Initiatives, a role aligned to the diversification agenda.
- [Registered office] CIN L51496GA1988PLC000915 indicates a Goa registration while all disclosed manufacturing is at Taloja, Maharashtra.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
